newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Bank Menatep, Inkombank ADRs delayed.
newsitem.headline: Russian Bank Menatep, Inkombank ADRs delayed.

text.p: Planned American Depositary Receipt (ADR) issues by two major Russian banks, Bank Menatep and Inkombank, have been delayed, bank officials said on Wednesday.
Both banks still intend to issue level-one ADRs in the near future, but an exact date has not yet been set, they said. They had intended to launch the certificates by the end of 1996.
A Menatep spokesman said the timetable had slipped because the bank was not treating the issue as a priority.
An Inkombank spokesman said the ADRs were being delayed by formalities.
One Menatep ADR will cover 10 underlying shares, and one Inkombank ADR will be equivalent to 15 shares.
Menatep has said its shares are worth around $2 each, while Inkombank says the shares are worth $0.80 each.
Bank shares are not actively traded in Russia, and the ADR issues would be the first way international portfolio investors could get access to the banks' stocks.

Inkombank has said it intends to place nine million ordinary shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles through the ADR issue, while Menatep wants to sell up to three percent of its authorised capital of 100 billion roubles.
Bank of New York will be the depositary bank for both programmes, and ING Bank Eurasia will be the custodian.
